doc:
Order-type-switch hide hook (`onHidden()` in UniFFI camelCase). OCO twin
of the stop-single `on_hidden`.

The Pure host swaps spot order-type panels via show/hide keep-alive, so a
hidden panel gets no Activity pause. Native re-inflates a fresh Fragment
per order-type and on the single vs double variant switch, showing a blank
draft each time. The typed draft lives in Rust state and survives
hide/show, so mirror native by clearing the input draft (BOTH OCO legs) on
this hide transition ONLY.

calls this ONLY when the hide is an in-container order-type / variant
switch (`!isHiddenByAncestor()`); a Home / Trade tab switch hides the
shell too, so it is NOT called and the draft is PRESERVED. Sibling parity
with `PureSpotLimitInteractor::on_hidden`.

Field set mirrors the canonical draft clear the panel already uses on a
side switch / pair switch / logout edge (`apply_side_state_mutation` +

seekbar.

variants.name: ShowTpslDirectionWarning
variants.doc:
TP/SL direction confirm dialog. Emitted by `submit_order` when the attached
TP/SL trigger sits on the wrong side of the entry (order) price; Kotlin shows an
OKDialog (continue / cancel).

**"Continue" KEEPS the attached TP/SL** — it only unlocks the gate and resumes the
BBO / pre-check / place pipeline with the frozen TP/SL payload intact
(`proceed_after_tpsl_direction_check_attempt`). This is a V2-only affordance on the
SPOT side and a deliberate divergence from the contract checker, which DOES drop
TP/SL on continue (`SwapAdvancedFragment.kt:854` / `SwapTriggerFragment.kt:571`
`group.sp = null; group.attachSp = null`, gated by
`OkTradeFuturePresent.checkSimpleTpSl`). Android Native has NO spot counterpart to
this dialog at all: `checkSimpleTpSl` / `checkAdvancedTpSl` are declared only on the
FUTURE presenter and every consumer is a contract fragment. The host states the same
contract in `SpotLimitDialogs.kt` ("Continue proceeds WITHOUT clearing TP/SL — spot
divergence from the contract checker").

The ONLY spot path that discards attached TP/SL is the server-price correction of the
51006 / 51137 / 51138 family (Native `OkTradePresenter.kt:1020` /
`OrderResultHandler.kt:233` `group.attachSp = null` after the user accepts the
suggested limit price) — see `pending_price_retry_discards_tpsl`, which is a
different trigger and a different lifecycle from this dialog. Do not conflate them.

(This doc previously claimed the continue path omits TP/SL from the submit snapshot,
which contradicted both the implementation and the host comment.)

`message` is the CDKey warning, resolved by
Kotlin via `DisplayString.resolve(ctx)`.

variants.doc:
Bug HH (2026-05-21) — limit-price-clipped dialog.

V1 reference (`RustSpotLimitTradePanelPresenter.kt:2048-2085` /
`OkTradePresenter.kt:1218-1219` /
`PreCheckResultHandler.kt:228-266`): when the BE returns a
"limit-price modify" error code (`LimitModifyError` aka the BE typo
`LIMIT_MIDIFY_ERROR`, `SpotMarginLimitPriceBuy`,
`SpotMarginLimitPriceSell`) the payload carries a server-suggested
`_data` price (the clipped allowed limit). V1 surfaces a confirmation
dialog asking the user to accept submission at the clipped price:
- BUY  -> `pr_options_placeorder_limit_modify_price` ("Your order
price triggered the limit. Confirm submitting at the maximum
allowed buy price {price}?")
- SELL -> `pr_trade_modal_order_sell_limit_modify_price` ("Your
order price triggered the limit. Confirm submitting at the
minimum allowed sell price {price}?")

Before this variant existed, the Rust make-order pipeline routed the
BE `LIMIT_MIDIFY_ERROR` family through `RouteCategory::ModifyOrderDialog`
→ `ShowOrderFailed` → Kotlin `SpotLimitDialogs.routeOrderFailed` Stage-1
toast (real-device-confirmed loop: user accepts local BBO → preCheck
passes → confirm dialog → submit → BE returns clipped error → no
dialog → user re-taps → local BBO fires again).

Confirm in the dialog routes through
[`PureSpotLimitActions::proceed_after_limit_price_clip`] which writes
`state.price = allowed_price` then re-runs `confirm_order` (skips the
local BBO + pre_check stages — those already passed; the clip is BE-side).
Cancel dismisses the dialog without any state mutation.
